summary: Source Workbench job writes distinguish validated confirmation from follow-up read failure. Optional version clearing sends null; required editing is never silently omitted. Matching valid job receipts and explicit true deletion gates precede local removal; confirmed deletion fences both collections, preserves other selection/editing and starts independent reads. Twenty-two real Chromium controls use mocked isolated services; ten real API and nine task-contract controls plus expanded JSON/SQLite regressions validate the backend separately. Ambiguous-write outcome reconciliation, installed GUIs, remote execution, power-loss, exactly-once, conflicts and large-history performance remain open. No persistent snapshots or production Node dependency are added.

required_text: deletion confirmation starts result recovery without waiting for a blocked job read
read recovery must not replay an ambiguous mutation
required identity checks never silently trim a nonblank identifier
explicit null clears optional version without changing execution or result
omitted version is unchanged and is distinct from clearing
confirmed job deletion removes its result, preserves other work and cannot be repeated
confirmed deletion stays committed when later collection reads lose storage
ten real API controls and nine direct task
